strategicPriorities.goal: Design and validate a sustainable provider/course-transaction revenue model. Do not enable live online payments before product, legal, support and technical gates pass.
Complete the real-backend migration and deterministic verification required to support the approved revenue and payment model safely.
Design student and provider support operations, especially registration, payment, refund and dispute escalation, before scale.
Prepare strategy and product prerequisites; do not run campaigns or spend budget until readiness gates are met.

governance.newAgentPolicy: Coordinator may propose a role. It may create and register the agent only after explicit project-owner approval.
teamReviewTriggers: after a major milestone is completed
when the same capability gap appears in at least two separate tasks or handoffs
when an existing agent repeatedly operates outside its declared scope
before entering payment, launch, or scaled support phases
governance.sourcePolicy: Use AITMPL as a base candidate, verify behaviour against current official Claude Code documentation, then rewrite for Qarğa's actual stack and business model.
governance.marketingPolicy: Strategy and readiness planning only until the project owner separately approves execution, publishing, ad spend, or external account access.
governance.performancePolicy: Evidence-based, non-zero-sum scorecards. Base points are assigned before execution; agents cannot self-score; proposals earn no points until approved and delivered.
performanceReviewTriggers: after every delegated deliverable that has acceptance criteria and evidence
at the end of a major milestone
when rolling quality drops below 70 after at least three tasks
when the same defect category appears twice

workflowRouting.fastLane: Normally 1-3 points and low risk: focused change, targeted check, diff review.
workflowRouting.standardLane: Normally 4-6 points or moderate risk: repository research, task contract, test-first work where practical, independent QA review, verification loop.
workflowRouting.criticalLane: Normally 7-10 points or any payment/auth/PII/legal/migration/production risk: owner gates, architecture and rollback, specialist reviews, full verification and milestone learning review.

governance.learningPolicy: Evidence-backed observations may become improvement proposals. No prompt, skill, hook, permission, plugin, agent, or permanent rule changes without coordinator review and the approvals defined in CLAUDE.md.
learningReviewTriggers: when the same defect or workflow failure appears twice
when a task-local workflow is successfully reused
when an agent enters a three-task improvement cycle
before payment, launch, or scaled-support stages
governance.projectMemoryPolicy: Approved decisions, concrete technical debt, and measurable experiments are stored in append-only project-memory registries. Records never override current repository evidence or newer explicit owner decisions.
projectMemoryReviewTriggers: at the start of every substantial coordinator session
before material product, revenue, payment, architecture, legal, security, or launch decisions
when repeated performance or learning signals may be explained by project history
governance.systemEvolutionPolicy: Persistent agent-system changes follow research → owner-approved proposal → qarga-system-improver → qarga-system-reviewer → pilot → KEEP/REVISE/REVERT. No silent self-modification.
governance.taskContractPolicy: Every delegated task uses a completion contract; accepted closure requires verified evidence and must not be anti-spin blocked.
governance.telemetryPolicy: Lifecycle telemetry is metadata-only and cannot contain prompts, secrets, personal data, or tool payloads.
governance.automationPolicy: Recurring 7/24 workers are disabled until project-owner approval, budget, permissions, secret management, kill switch, and no-auto-merge/deploy rules are configured.
governance.workOsPolicy: Delegated and multi-step work is represented in Qarğa Work OS as persistent parent tasks and independently reviewable subtasks. The coordinator owns decomposition and assignment; specialists cannot self-assign, self-score, or mark their own work done. Dependencies, owner-decision gates, completion contracts, independent review, performance scoring, and activity history must stay linked.
workOsReviewTriggers: at the start of every substantial coordinator session
before delegating a multi-step or multi-agent deliverable
when an owner decision, blocker, or dependency changes
after independent review closes a subtask
governance.skillEvolutionPolicy: Repeated Work OS/performance evidence may trigger read-only skill research. Skill/prompt candidates require existing-skill inventory, failed-attempt review, anti-overfitting analysis, independent baseline-vs-candidate validation and hidden holdout, critical regression gates, and a minimum three-real-task pilot before permanent promotion.
skillEvolutionTriggers: same capability defect appears in at least two independent real-work signals
an agent enters an improvement cycle and a reusable capability gap is suspected
a reusable successful pattern has evidence across multiple tasks
a system change proposes a new or materially edited skill or agent prompt

learningTracking.promotionPolicy: Persistent changes require evidence, coordinator review, required specialist review, and explicit project-owner approval where defined.

systemEvaluation.policy: Agent-system changes require deterministic checks, fresh-context regression review, and the approvals defined in CLAUDE.md.

projectMemory.authority: Project memory never overrides current repository evidence, CLAUDE.md, or newer explicit project-owner decisions.
